statement: You manage all your store's payment methods in the Payment providers area of Shopify.

To accept credit cards through a provider other than Shopify Payments, choose from over 100 credit card payment providers for your Shopify store. You can use a third-party provider as your sole credit card processor, or you can use it alongside Shopify Payments to access additional payment methods such as Shop Pay and local payment methods.

Shopify supports two different types of credit card payment providers: direct providers and external providers. If you're using a direct provider, then your customers can complete their purchases directly on your online store without having to pay at a third-party checkout. If you're using an external provider, then your customers must complete their purchases on a checkout page that's hosted outside of your online store.

identifier: Using Shopify Payments with a third-party provider
statement: You can use Shopify Payments alongside a direct third-party payment provider in the same store. In this setup, your third-party provider is the primary processor for credit and debit card transactions, and Shopify Payments handles additional payment methods your third-party provider doesn't support, such as Shop Pay and local payment methods.

* Your store must be in a country where Shopify Payments is supported. * You must have an active direct third-party payment provider configured in your store. * Merchants on the Shopify Plus plan who already use Shop Pay Express can continue using Shop Pay Express until their Plus contract becomes eligible for Shopify Payments alongside a third-party provider. Merchants on the Shopify Plus plan with signed contracts, including new merchants and merchants renewing their contracts, aren't eligible to use Shopify Payments alongside a third-party provider at this time. * This feature isn't available in multi-entity setups. Only Shopify Payments can be used as a direct provider in multi-entity setups.
You can use only one direct third-party payment provider alongside Shopify Payments at a time.

statement: Payment recovery is automatically activated when you use Shopify Payments alongside a direct third-party payment provider. It isn't configurable and can't be deactivated.
Shop Pay Express is being replaced by the ability to use Shopify Payments alongside your third-party provider. What happens depends on your Shopify plan:

* The Basic, Shopify, and Advanced plans: Your store is automatically migrated to the new model. Your rates decrease and you gain access to additional Shopify Payments features, including wallet and local payment methods not offered by your third-party provider. Payment recovery is automatically activated for eligible card transactions. Wallet and local payment methods aren't automatically activated after migration. No action is required to maintain access to Shop Pay. * The Shopify Plus plan, terms of service: You need to opt in through your Shopify admin and accept updated terms before migration is complete. * The Shopify Plus plan, contract: You retain access to Shop Pay Express until your Plus contract becomes eligible for this feature.

identifier: How a merchant installs a payments extension
statement: 1. The payments app is installed by merchants directly through an installation link that's shared by the payments developer, or through Shopify's public list of payment gateways in the Shopify admin. 2. The merchant installs the app on the OAuth grant page. 3. The merchant is redirected to the payments app page to configure the payments app settings. Until configuration is complete, a banner indicates that the provider isn't ready to process payments. 4. The merchant configures the payments app. 5. The app marks itself as ready by calling the Shopify API. 6. Shopify enables the app to be activated by the merchant in the Shopify admin. 7. The merchant activates the app. 8. The merchant deactivates the legacy payment gateway to avoid duplicate payment methods during checkout, if applicable.

Designation. From time to time Shopify may allow payment providers to become a Payments Developer and permit them to develop a Payments Application. A payment provider can apply to become a Payments Developer through the Payments Platform Onboarding Form.

If a Payments Application meets the criteria set out in the Payments Platform Developer Guidelines for public listing by Shopify, the Payments Developer may apply to Shopify for a public listing. Shopify will review such Payments Applications and depending on a number of factors determined and assessed by Shopify in its sole discretion, including transaction volume and Payments Application adoption rates, Shopify may approve the Payments Application inclusion in Shopify’s public list of payment gateways and make the Payments Application available to Merchants via Merchants admin. Shopify reserves the right to (1) conduct periodic reviews to ensure Payments Applications continue to meet the requirements for public listing and (2) remove from public listing such Payments Applications that no longer meet the requirements.

If a Payments Application is not approved for public listing , the Payments Developer may permit Merchants to install the Payments Application, by providing Merchants with a shareable installation link.

New Payments Application Feature Approval. Any updates or changes to an existing Payments Application, including the addition of new product features or new payment methods, must be submitted for review and approval.

Merchant Flexibility. Payments Applications must allow for Shopify Merchants to terminate their agreement with the payment provider within 7 days’ notice, without any penalty, fine, or other consequence.
Settlements. All Payments Applications must settle transactions for the Merchants within a maximum of 5 days, as outlined in the Payments Platform Developer Guidelines.

During the Wind Down Period, both Parties will continue to perform their obligations under this agreement and Payments Developer will continue to support and maintain any Payments Application for Merchants, such that all existing functionalities remain in effect. The Parties will collaborate in good faith and agree on a transition plan for the Merchants using any Payments Application that will go into effect at the end of the Wind Down Period and Payments Developer will be responsible to provide notice to Merchants notifying them as to the expected date that any Payments Application will no longer be available for use.
